title: When a Curitiba Pharmacy Began Making Its Own Creams
conflicts: Which shop was the first franchise: Mercado & Consumo calls the 1979 airport shop the first franchise, the company's Portuguese site calls it the first exclusive shop, Jornal de Brasília and SuperVarejo put the start of franchising in 1980 (Brasília), and the company's US blog says 1982. The story calls the airport shop the brand's own and starts the franchise network in Brasília in 1980. The first product lists differ in detail between the company site and Jornal de Brasília, so the story says 'a few creams'.
notes: Sourcing is thinner than ideal: Krigsner gave few interviews before his 2024 book, so the founder's voice comes from one Brazil Journal interview (one Portuguese quotation, glossed in English) and the early details (Porto Alegre course, shop interior, sister's mixer) are the company's own history, attributed as such. The US$3,000 and 1975 degree are Bloomberg Línea's only. Several otherwise useful pages (Forbes Brasil, Bem Paraná) return 403 and were not used. Slate industry 'pharmaceuticals' changed to cosmetics, which is what the episode is about.
